prompt: A particle moves along a line with position $s(t) = t^3 - 6t^2 + 9t$ meters at time $t$ seconds. Find its velocity at $t = 4$ seconds, in meters per second.
hint: Velocity is the derivative of position. Differentiate term by term.

hints.text: Velocity is the derivative of position. Differentiate term by term.

explanation: $= 9$ m/s. Positive, so the particle is moving in the positive direction at $t = 4$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Where was it stopped?
steps: Factor the velocity: $3t^2 - 12t + 9 = 3(t - 1)(t - 3)$, which is zero at $t = 1$ and $t = 3$.
Between $1$ and $3$ the velocity is negative (the particle backs up); after $t = 3$ it is positive again.
